correctness.rationale: For all n=7k>=7 the canonical seven-column pattern is an RDF of weight 8k. Every RDF is exactly a closed walk in the 6561-state transfer digraph, with cost 7w-8n. A full finite verification of all 48681 arcs produces an integer potential with nonnegative reduced costs and a tight-edge digraph whose only cyclic SCC is a directed seven-cycle. Equality therefore forces repetition of the seven pattern and exactly seven shifts; direct residue comparisons give pairwise Hamming distance 8k. Two separately written critical-SCC implementations and independent order-7/order-14 enumeration were replayed.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparison with the two most relevant Roman-domination papers separates prior optimal-weight and transfer-graph theorems from the new equality-case rigidity. The new result relies on an independently established unique tight cycle, rather than claiming that a literature search proves priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed enumeration of minimum Roman dominating functions for the P(n,2) family might independently state the same sevenfold rigidity.
The 2014 transfer formulation might permit a different unpublished or implicit exact tight-cycle computation; its published theorems do not state that computation.
No independent external verification of originality or the finite certificate has been performed.

value.rationale: A classification of all optimizers in an infinite natural graph family is structurally stronger than the known optimum weight. Constant sevenfold degeneracy and linearly increasing pairwise separation demonstrate rigid periodic equality and motivate the exact critical-cycle calculation; the result is neither a textbook deduction from the value formula nor a single arbitrary small census.
